clue.text: The approach to landing in London

definitions.text: The approach to landing in London

parts.words: The approach to landing in London
parts.note: the way up to an upstairs landing is a flight of stairs, and in London's Cockney rhyming slang stairs are called by a pair of fruits

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it; 'in London' points to that East End slang, and 'landing' is the top of a staircase, not an aircraft touching down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for stairs, which are what lead up to a landing.

clue.text: Mountaineer's requirement to start pulling 20 cwt

indicators.note: the start of the word pulling is its opening letter

parts.note: twenty hundredweight make one imperial ton, written I (one) and TON

explanation.surface: A climber needs to begin hauling a load weighing a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundredweight (cwt) is an old British unit; twenty of them make one ton, so the figure is read as I TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber hammers this metal spike into rock to secure a rope.

clue.text: The early bird and the paper man played around

parts.note: the lark is the proverbial early riser among birds
the editor is the man in charge of a newspaper, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A dawn bird and a newspaper boss fooled about together.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to fool around or play pranks.

clue.text: The wheels needed to put fish on the slab?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish
a board is a flat slab of wood

explanation.surface: A fishmonger asks what is needed to lay fish out on the counter slab.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'wheels' means a vehicle, here a wheeled plank for riding.

clue.text: Crazy students drinking time

indicators.note: the union drinking something takes it inside, so the time letter goes into the students' abbreviation

parts.note: NUS is the UK's National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Students spending all their time drinking are mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal for mad or insane.

clue.text: Fish pie unfinished — managed to have half

indicators.note: an unfinished word loses its final letter, so pie is cut short

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so managed gives RAN

indicators.note: half of the word have means its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone left a fish pie half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'half' works on the neighbouring word 'have', giving HA.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American freshwater fish with razor-sharp teeth.

clue.text: Saddler at work on rider's stance

indicators.note: the letters of saddler and at are put to work, i.e. reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A saddle-maker is busy with how a horse rider sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on each side, as a rider sits a horse.

clue.text: Drunken Scot sold beer? No — not at all!

indicators.note: drunken letters stagger about, so Scot, sold, beer and no are rearranged

explanation.surface: Was a Scotsman sold beer and so got drunk? No, quite the reverse!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: 'not at all' drunk, which is the answer's meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely sober means not drunk in the slightest, the reverse of the Scot in the surface.

clue.text: Uninformed ideas about procreation

definitions.meaning: opinions formed in advance, before knowing the facts
read playfully as things coming before conceiving a baby

explanation.definitionFit: Prejudged notions, formed ahead of knowledge; split as pre-conception it means before a baby is conceived.

clue.text: Delaying outburst about trade problem

indicators.note: the rant goes about, i.e. around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: a rant is an angry outburst

indicators.note: a problem with trade means its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A furious outburst about a trade difficulty holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire retardant substance slows down or hinders burning.

clue.text: Proportion spending a time in port

indicators.note: a and the time letter are placed in the port's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A sailor spends some time ashore in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a quantitative relation between two amounts.

clue.text: Summon the prisoner — even for display

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: putting even on display arranges its letters differently

explanation.surface: Call the convict in, even just for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link before the anagram indicator 'display'.
explanation.definitionFit: To call a meeting or assembly together.

clue.text: One meant to correspond with prisoner

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the letters of meant are made to correspond, rearranged to match a new word

explanation.surface: Someone was supposed to write letters to a jailed man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined in a jail or institution.

clue.text: The spirit failed, we hear, to provide illusion

parts.note: Scotch whisky is a spirit

indicators.note: signals that the word for failed is taken by its sound only

parts.note: to have missed is to have failed to hit

explanation.surface: A drinker's spirits fail them, and they see things that are not there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide' is a link. Scotch mist is a British idiom for something imaginary, as in 'what do you think that is, Scotch mist?'
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something imaginary or not really there.

clue.text: Bouquet delivered to the front of the plane

definitions.meaning: the forward tip of an aircraft's fuselage

explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered to' is a link; 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but it is the wine-taster's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's smell, and also the pointed forward section of an aircraft.

clue.text: Chew over and risk an investment

definitions.meaning: to ponder or think about something at length
to buy shares hoping for a profitable rise

explanation.definitionFit: To theorize about a matter, and to gamble money on markets.

clue.text: Dicey game of tick?

definitions.meaning: tick, or tag, is a playground game where one child touches another and runs off

explanation.definitionFit: A precarious situation; also, literally, what happens in tag: tap someone and then run.

clue.text: House filler

parts.note: the House of Commons is filled with members chosen by the body of voters

explanation.walkthrough: 'House' means not a home but the House of Commons, whose seats are filled by voters at an election.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of voters, who choose who sits in Parliament.

clue.text: The Italian, in future perhaps, can be stretched

indicators.note: the Italian article goes in the grammatical term

parts.note: the future is an example of a grammatical tense
il is Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: An Italian man can stretch out in times to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensile describes material capable of being drawn out or extended.

clue.text: Join in lewd play

indicators.note: putting lewd into play moves its letters about

explanation.surface: Take part in some saucy fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse metal pieces together with heat.

clue.text: Rubbish left under motor

indicators.note: in a down clue the left letter sits below the motor word

parts.note: to motor is to drive a car

explanation.surface: Garbage has been dumped beneath a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is nonsense, silly talk.

clue.text: Mainly faithful worker may play hookey

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: true means loyal or faithful
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A mostly loyal employee might skive off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing hookey' is American slang for skipping school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who skips school without permission, i.e. one who may play hookey.

clue.text: Nelson's house? 11

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, the word for a proportion

explanation.surface: Is this the admiral's home? See clue 11.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelson's' means Nelson's first name: Admiral Lord Nelson was christened with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of Admiral Lord Nelson, Britain's naval hero.

clue.text: Belief that energy is absorbed by canvas

indicators.note: the energy letter is taken into the canvas shelter

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone believes that a canvas sail soaks up power.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held as true.

clue.text: Therefore return the monster

indicators.note: the word for therefore comes back, read from its end

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: So the monster comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of fairy tales.

clue.text: Middle eastern merit award given to a province

parts.note: the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour
Northern Ireland is often called the Province, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: An honour for merit is bestowed on a region of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link; 'the Province' is a common British name for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to Oman, a country on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Vegan rice freak with a grudge

indicators.note: freak signals the letters of vegan and rice are to be thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A rice-loving vegan has a bone to pick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' is a link; 'freak' looks like a noun for an enthusiast, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint or resentment held against someone.

clue.text: Does it make gentility seem a particular obsession?

indicators.note: to make a word out of gentility, seem and a, rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: Asks whether refined manners appear to be a fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive mindset of feeling under constant attack: a particular kind of fixation.
